column1: Abbreviations: AICc, corrected Akaike information criterion; ARIMA, autoregressive integrated moving average; HF, heart failure; IHD, ischemic heart disease; NH, non-Hispanic; PE, pulmonary embolism; RMSE, root mean square error. Annual mortality rates from 1999 through 2023 (25 observations per series) were modeled. Age-group models used age-specific mortality rates; all other models used age-adjusted mortality rates. Nonseasonal ARIMA models were selected by stepwise minimization of AICc, with nonseasonal differencing determined using the KPSS procedure (maximum p and q, 5; maximum d, 2; p + q ≤ 5). If the initial automatic model showed residual autocorrelation (Ljung-Box P < .05) or generated any negative point forecast from 2024 through 2040, candidate models with the same differencing order were evaluated, and the lowest-AICc model satisfying Ljung-Box P ≥ .05 and nonnegative point forecasts was retained. Residual autocorrelation was assessed using the Ljung-Box test at lag 10, with degrees of freedom calculated as 10 − (p + q). Forecast accuracy was evaluated using 10 rolling-origin, one-step-ahead cross-validation folds, with the selected model specification refitted at each forecast origin. Raw 95% prediction limits are reported. Analyses were performed in Python 3.13.5 using statsforecast 2.0.3. Forecasts are conditional model-based projections and should not be interpreted as deterministic predictions.
